notes:
Summary: VertexCraft is building a VS Code copilot extension focused on low-latency streaming completions and in-line suggestions for mid-sized developer teams. They want a reproducible model pin + rollback story so users get deterministic completions across releases. Key asks: 30-60ms median suggestion latency (when running hosted in us-west), per-extension API keys with per-user and per-seat rate limiting, and SSO/SAML + SCIM for provisioning.

POC scope (2 weeks): instrument extension to measure end-to-end latency (editor -> websocket -> Redwood -> token returned -> render), evaluate streaming chunk size for smoother UX, validate model-version pin and automatic fallback to smaller quantized model when capacity constrained. They also want sample client SDK patterns to batch low-priority completion telemetry to avoid rate spikes.

Security/Compliance notes: legal flagged telemetry retention and telemetry sampling — want explicit retention_controls and opt-out flag for users. IdP SAML metadata exchange outstanding; also asked about KMS integration for secrets in Dedicated. Redwood provided SOC2 report and draft audit_logging SLA.

Technical preferences & constraints: prefer hosted_api in initial rollouts for fastest iteration; dedicated for enterprise customers inside VPC later. Edge routing for EU users — data residency concerns for enterprise pilot. They emphasized model/version pinning to ensure reproducibility for regression tests. They asked about offline dev mode: ability to run a quantized local model during network outages (nice-to-have).

Quotes / call snippets: "Need suggestions to feel instant — if it lags, devs shrug and stop using it." — eng lead. "We need a clear billing forecast for token spikes from streaming sessions." — finance.

Next steps (short): SE to deliver POC perf dashboard by 2026-03-12, security questionnaire answers by 2026-03-15, follow-up review with product on model-pin rollback UX. If POC meets latency and security bar, forecast for Dedicated contract for enterprise pilot in 2026-06.
